audits.title: 506 An Audit of Documentation in Orthopaedic Trauma Meetings
audits.standard: Academy of Medical Royal Colleges and British Orthopaedic Association record keeping standards
audits.setting: Trauma and orthopaedics, Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust, London

cycle1.result: Most had trauma meeting documentation but often lacked take consultant, injury, date/mechanism and contact details.

audits.intervention: Trauma meeting documentation proforma.

cycle2.result: 70% or above for documentation of significant information in almost all criteria.

audits.other_findings: Poor documentation led to repeated calls to the on-call team to clarify plans.
audits.citation: Jackson T, Chahal J. 506 An Audit of Documentation in Orthopaedic Trauma Meetings. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_2). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab134.440.

audits.title: 469 Improving the Quality of Trauma Meeting Documentation
audits.standard: Eight documentation standards: consultant on-call, consultants present, imaging discussed, MDT concerns, diagnosis, laterality, clear plan, weight-bearing status
audits.setting: Trauma meeting, Wythenshawe Hospital, Manchester

cycle1.result: Only 64% of cases discussed had documentation.

audits.intervention: Structured electronic smart-phrase proforma, adjusted after MDT feedback.

cycle2.result: 88% of cases discussed were documented; all eight standards improved.

audits.other_findings: PDSA 2 (n=98) documented 94%; lack of consultant time to complete documentation was highlighted.

audits.title: Standardised proformas improve patient handover: Audit of trauma handover practice.
audits.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England 'Safe Handover' minimum dataset and BMA guidance; gold standard 100% data transmission and 100% proforma compliance
audits.setting: Department of Trauma and Orthopaedics, University Hospital of Wales, Cardiff (teaching hospital), on-call handover

cycle1.result: Handwritten plain paper sheets: patient labels used 73% (35/48); side of injury handed over in 28/49; tasks performed or outstanding 31% (15); relevant blood results 19% (6/32); overall data handed over 72.6%.

audits.intervention: Standardised handover proforma based on the RCS dataset, piloted (version 1, 78% compliance), revised after junior doctor feedback and implemented as version 2.

cycle2.result: 100% proforma compliance; labels 96% (53/55); side of injury 98% (54/55); tasks 100% (55/55); relevant blood results 20% (6/29); overall data handed over 93.2% (p<0.01).

audits.other_findings: Handover of relevant blood results stayed poor, possibly because the form had no dedicated field for it. The abstract reports label use as 72.9% to 93.4%.
audits.citation: Ferran NA, Metcalfe AJ, O'Doherty D. Standardised proformas improve patient handover: Audit of trauma handover practice. Patient Saf Surg. 2008;2:24. doi:10.1186/1754-9493-2-24. PMID: 18817559.

audits.title: Using a proforma to improve standards of documentation of an orthopaedic post-take ward round.
audits.standard: GMC and Royal College of Physicians documentation recommendations: clearly documented PTWR, date/time, consultant on take, clinician leading and documenting, presenting complaint and management plan
audits.setting: District general hospital trauma and orthopaedic department (population 320,000, consultant-led 24/7 trauma service)

cycle1.result: 72% seen on PTWR, 47% of these clearly labelled; 64% of those not seen were weekend admissions; no consultant on take identifiable in 19%, presenting complaint missing in 78%, no plan in 3%, not timed in 17%, no name 19%, no signature 14%, no grade 50%, no contact details 25%.

audits.intervention: Trauma Meeting/Post-Take Ward Round proforma on yellow paper, designed with the team (PDSA cycles), results presented at departmental teaching, and weekend surgical juniors briefed to attend the trauma meeting and complete it.

cycle2.period: Prospective re-audit two weeks after implementation
cycle2.result: Not seen on PTWR fell from 28% to 18% (4% weekend admissions); 88% of those seen had a proforma; 18% of all cases had no proforma; consultant unidentifiable in 4%; all entries signed and dated; no name 12%, no contact details 15%, no grade 10%.

audits.other_findings: Weekend proforma completion stayed poor (67% of cases without a proforma were weekend admissions); all remaining documentation gaps were in cases without a proforma.
audits.citation: Duxbury O, Hili S, Afolayan J. Using a proforma to improve standards of documentation of an orthopaedic post-take ward round. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2013;2(1):u200902.w699. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u200902.w699. PMID: 26734180.

audits.title: Improving handover of acute orthopaedic admissions.
audits.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England handover guidance (2007) plus local orthopaedic-specific criteria
audits.setting: Trauma unit, Ulster Hospital, Dundonald (district general hospital)

cycle1.result: Poor handover: patient location 57%, responsible consultant 14%, results of significant/pending investigations 29%, co-morbidities 38%, outstanding tasks 38%; one patient not handed over and one nerve injury not handed over.

audits.intervention: Trauma-specific paper handover proforma (SHOs informed by email and verbally), then an electronic proforma accessible from any hospital computer, created with IT.

cycle2.result: With the electronic proforma only one criterion fell below 95% (results of pending investigations 82%); no patient safety issues; proforma uptake 100%.

audits.other_findings: Intermediate re-audit with the paper proforma (10/02/15 to 16/02/15, 19 patients in text, 17 in abstract): management plan 76%, results of investigations 47%, outstanding tasks 71%, all other criteria at least 80%.
audits.citation: Karayiannis P, Warnock J. Improving handover of acute orthopaedic admissions. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2015;4(1):u209209.w3901. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u209209.w3901. PMID: 26734416.

audits.title: Making the weekend work: a local quality improvement project to establish and improve the quality of weekend handover.
audits.standard: 10 handover components derived from RCS, RCP and BMA handover guidelines, each with a set standard (some patient identifiers at 100%); aim to raise compliance to 90–100%
audits.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedics department, Frimley Park Hospital (750-bed NHS hospital), Surrey

cycle1.result: Baseline (247 handovers over nine weeks): patient name 99%, hospital number 94%, admission reason 91%, other categories 12% to 84% (date of birth 54%, location 84%, frequency of review 70%, TTO 12%); only admission reason met its standard.

audits.intervention: Two-step change: extra columns (TTO, day to be seen, DNAR) added to the Word handover table, then a new intranet handover tool with drop-down boxes, date selector and multiuser access; instruction document given at induction.

cycle2.result: Sustainability re-audit of intranet tool (201 handovers, new cohort of doctors): patient name 100%, hospital number 98%, date of birth 85%; five of 10 categories met their standard (patient name, location, consultant, admission reason, frequency of review); all except TTO were above 50%.

audits.other_findings: After the amended table (257 handovers) TTO rose from 12% to 31% and location fell from 84% to 77%; after the intranet tool (207 handovers) location 90%, consultant 94%, admission reason 97%, frequency of review 100% and TTO 5%. TTO stayed poorest (18%) and was dropped from the tool.
audits.citation: Heller RA, Hu L. Making the weekend work: a local quality improvement project to establish and improve the quality of weekend handover. BMJ Open Qual. 2018;7(3):e000215. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2017-000215. PMID: 30094343.

audits.title: Designing a new orthopaedic trauma meeting proforma to improve documentation in a large UK teaching hospital.
audits.standard: Locally designed trauma meeting documentation standards (no UK guideline exists); record keeping guidance from GMC, RCS England and BMA
audits.setting: Trauma and orthopaedic department, Wythenshawe Hospital, Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust (acute teaching hospital)

cycle1.result: 58/90 (64%) had some documentation. Consultant on call 43%, other consultants 29%, imaging 20%, MDT concerns 7%, diagnosis 29%, laterality 22%, clear plan 63%, weight-bearing 1%.

audits.intervention: Electronic trauma meeting proforma (EPR shortcut) introduced, then revised after MDT feedback (theatre checklist added); teaching video and poster for new doctors before the one-year re-audit.

cycle2.result: 71/85 (84%) had some documentation. Consultant on call, other consultants and imaging 100%, diagnosis 97%, laterality 75%, clear plan 98%.

audits.other_findings: Phase 2 (11 to 20 October 2022, n=98) reached 94% documentation; phase 3 (20 to 30 October 2022, n=108) 88%, with only 6/57 (11%) completing the new theatre checklist. Weight-bearing and MDT concerns sections were later removed.
audits.citation: Warrington DJ, Yip CR, Kassir A, Nadar N, Elcock K, Peach C. Designing a new orthopaedic trauma meeting proforma to improve documentation in a large UK teaching hospital. Ann R Coll Surg Engl. 2026;108(3):207-213. doi:10.1308/rcsann.2025.0043. PMID: 40702969.

audits.title: Quality of Trauma Meeting Presentations Before and After Introduction of a Structured Template at a Major Trauma Centre: A Before-and-After Quality Improvement Study.
audits.standard: Locally developed 10-domain, 20-point presentation quality score; complete presentation defined a priori as score ≥ 16
audits.setting: Morning trauma meeting, Department of Trauma and Orthopaedics, major trauma centre (Salford Royal NHS Foundation Trust)

cycle1.result: Mean score 11.6 ± 3.0/20; complete presentations 18/75 (24.0%); management plan documented 49/75 (65.3%); tasks allocated 28/75 (37.3%); median clarification prompts 2 (IQR 1-3).

audits.intervention: One-page 10-domain structured presentation template expanded from an acronym in the electronic patient record, introduced with a five-minute briefing, laminated copies in the meeting room and inclusion in the junior doctor induction pack.

cycle2.result: Mean score 17.1 ± 2.1/20 (difference 5.5, 95% CI 4.7-6.3; p<0.001); complete presentations 61/75 (81.3%; p<0.001); management plan 72/75 (96.0%); tasks allocated 67/75 (89.3%); median clarification prompts 1 (IQR 0-1).

audits.other_findings: Median presentation duration unchanged (2.7 to 2.5 minutes, p=0.18); neurovascular status improved from 34/75 (45.3%) to 66/75 (88.0%). Sustainability beyond the initial period was not assessed.
audits.citation: Ahmed H, Rizwan M, Alnsour AAM, Rehman A, Ammar MS, Ijaz M. Quality of Trauma Meeting Presentations Before and After Introduction of a Structured Template at a Major Trauma Centre: A Before-and-After Quality Improvement Study. Cureus. 2026;18(6):e111299. doi:10.7759/cureus.111299. PMID: 42488269.
